عُوقٌ A man in whom, (O,) or with whom, (K,) is no good; (O, K;) as also ↓ عَوْقٌ ; (K;) occurring in the saying of Ru-beh, “فِدَاكَ مِنْهُمْ كُلُّ عَوْقٍ أَصْلَدُ
” [May every one of them in whom, or with whom, is no good, who is niggardly, be thy ransom]: (TA:) pl. أَعْوَاقٌ. (K.) ―
-b2- See also عَائِقٌ.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
